narrative.overview:
In a telephone exchange, the main distribution frame is the steel rack where every subscriber line lands on one side, every switch port on the other, and jumper wire crosses between them. It is the act of routing made into an object: who connects to whom is not described anywhere, it is visible as wire. This site is that frame.

The ground is equipment enamel, the warm putty of painted exchange steel under fluorescent light. Structure is painted steel members at one and two pixels; text is engraved ink; labels ride on designation-strip stock. The only chromatic system is the 25-pair telecom colour code, spent exclusively on live jumper wire.

The system is entirely flat and entirely square: zero box-shadows, zero backdrop-filters, and exactly one border-radius — the 50% on the rivet dots at the ends of each designation strip. Depth is real material stacking, never simulated relief.
keyCharacteristics: Equipment-enamel ground; no dark mode, no glass, no gradient field
The 25-pair colour code as the only chroma, reserved for wire
Square corners everywhere; one circle, on the strip rivets
No shadows and no blur — depth from tonal grounds and steel members
Full-bleed frame elevation; no centred content column
Data set in mono with tabular figures; prose in Archivo
One authored landing: strips seat, then jumpers run, then it stops

rules.name: The Wire Rule
rules.body: The 25-pair colour code is spent on jumper wire and on the legend that decodes it. Nothing else may take a pair colour — not a button, chip, border or focus ring. A page where the accent appears on controls is one where a blue wire reads as brand colour instead of as pair 1.

rules.name: The Fill Rule
rules.body: State is carried by fill and weight, never by hue. Live is ink-filled with strip type; dimmed recedes to the enamel ground. Never dim with opacity: a translucent chip lets jumper wire show through and reads as a strike-through.

rules.name: The No-Pure-Black Rule
rules.body: The darkest value is Ink (#191b17). Pure #000 and #fff never appear.

rules.name: The Instrument Voice Rule
rules.body: If a value was measured, counted, dated or rated, it is mono with tabular figures. If a human wrote it as a sentence, or it is the name of a thing, it is Archivo. A technology name is a label, not a reading.

rules.name: The Engraved Strip Rule
rules.body: A designation strip never truncates. Below 560px it drops its clause and shows the designation alone.

rules.name: The Shared Member Rule
rules.body: Adjacent units share one steel member. Two abutting 1px borders read as a 2px seam and turn a block back into a stack of cards.

rules.name: The Full-Bleed Rule
rules.body: The frame owns the whole viewport. No centred column, no content max-width. The upright rail is the only reserved edge.

rules.name: The No-Relief Rule
rules.body: Never simulate the material. No bevels, emboss, metallic gradient or grain. Real material arrives as a produced raster, not as CSS relief. Imitation material is the most reliable mark of machine-made design.

rules.name: The Three Plane Rule
rules.body: Every surface is raised (enamel-lit), recessed (trough), or strip stock. Name its plane before building it.

rules.name: The Square Rule
rules.body: Nothing is rounded. If a new element seems to want a radius, it wants a different plane or member weight instead. The single circle is the 5px strip rivet.

dos: Do spend the 25-pair colour code on wire and its legend, and nowhere else.
Do carry state with fill and weight — ink-filled for live, outline for at-rest, receded to enamel for dimmed.
Do keep every surface square. The one circle is the 5px strip rivet.
Do name a surface's plane before building it: raised, recessed, or strip stock.
Do let adjacent units share one steel member.
Do set every measured value in mono with tabular figures and a slashed zero.
Do derive relationships from the record — a wire may only exist where the CV already says it does.
Do keep the frame full-bleed; the upright rail is the only reserved edge.
Do put an interactive control on an actual button and leave headings as headings.
donts: Don't give a pair colour to a button, chip, border or focus ring.
Don't add a box-shadow or a backdrop-filter. There are zero of each, deliberately.
Don't dim with opacity — a translucent terminal lets wire show through and reads as a strike-through.
Don't simulate the material with CSS bevels, emboss, metallic gradients or grain.
Don't centre the content in a column, or re-introduce a hero above the identification strip.
Don't ship a big-number-plus-small-label stat row. Counts belong on designation strips and in the frame data panel.
Don't let a designation strip truncate; drop its clause instead.
Don't print the same record at two designations. One record, one home.
Don't wrap a whole card in role="button". It swallows the headings inside it and destroys the document outline.
